FLUX CAPITAL
DEAL SUMMARY
American Housing Corp.
The American Housing Corporation (AHC) is a vertically-integrated
homebuilder + housing manufacturer designed to solve "missing
middle" housing at scale via (i) a standardized rowhome format, (ii) a
factory-manufactured componentized building system that fits in
standard shipping containers, and (iii) an internal software layer
(Alamo) to run underwriting → production → onsite assembly.

THE OPPORTUNITY
Residential construction has not meaningfully benefited from industrial-scale productivity improvements, despite a
persistent housing shortage and structurally high construction costs. AHC's thesis is that the path to scale is not
"modular houses as a product," but a repeatable, software-orchestrated manufacturing + assembly system that
can be deployed across geographies with predictable cost, timeline, and quality.
AHC's approach is componentized (e.g., bathrooms/kitchens + panels) and built for factory repeatability; each
module is designed to fit standard shipping containers for cost-efficient logistics and national deployment. That
production line is married with a software layer (Alamo) as the "manufacturing OS." Alamo is intended to manage
underwriting, site planning, factory production, and onsite assembly-creating a compounding operational dataset
and tighter feedback loops than contractor-led construction.
AHC is explicitly structuring the business so real estate capital can fund land + builds (PropCo) while the
venture-backed OpCo captures high-margin manufacturing + system IP-aligning the capital stack with the
growth bottleneck (production capacity) for efficient scaling.
AHC is raising $50M to build out their first "Gigafactory" that will enable AHC to drive costs lower, expand
margins, and scale production from dozens of units a year to over a thousand. The Series A round is fully
subscribed and led by Contrary Ventures. Our participation in their Seed round and leading their last Bridge round
gives our LPs exclusive access to allocation.
